jobs.description: Employer: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Expires: 11/26/2026 Research and Development (R&D) at Procter & Gamble, the largest consumer packaged goods company in the world, includes a diverse group of roles that contribute to the innovation and development of our products. It encompasses roles in product research, formulation, testing, and scientific analysis. You will find variety and excitement starting Day 1. This internship is specifically designed for individuals working towards a PhD who are developing proficiency in their field. As an intern or co-op in management, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals in a supportive environment. This is a 12-week paid internship, designed to provide you with a solid foundation for future career growth. The internship will take place from May (potentially early June) to August of 2027. Join us at P&G, where your contributions will play a vital role in shaping the future of consumer products! The Opportunity:P&G has an opportunity for a PhD intern to work in our Corporate R&D to develop an AI-agent-driven framework that automates and accelerates machine learning experimentation for time-series data modeling. The intern will explore how AI agents can propose and execute experiments, modify configurations or code, analyze results, and recommend next steps. This work will investigate improvements in data preprocessing, model architecture, training strategies, and hyperparameter selection while comparing AI-driven research with conventional experimentation in terms of model performance, reproducibility, and research efficiency.The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong eagerness to learn and grow professionally and possess excellent communication skills—both written and verbal. This role is perfect for those with passion for innovation and problem-solving, along with a proactive attitude and the ability to adapt to new challenges. Join us in this dynamic environment, where your contributions will make a real impact as part of a collaborative team! Available to work 5 days a week in office at Mason, OH location. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with large language models, generative AI, and the design of multi-step agentic workflows or multi-agent systems.Experience with agentic frameworks such as LangGraph and AI observability platforms such as Arize.Experience with automated machine learning, hyperparameter optimization, experiment orchestration, or experiment-tracking systems.Experience in time-series data modeling.A record of research contributions through grants, fellowships, patents, peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, or relevant open-source projects. The fellow will be trained by a supportive team of scientists who participate in established regional and national exposure-assessment studies. This training opportunity focuses on the analysis of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in blood and other matrices using equilibrium headspace gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS).The training will include:Developing, implementing, and troubleshooting biological specimen collection and handling procedures for the accurate analysis of VOCs at low parts-per-trillion concentrations using GC/MS and automated approachesOptimizing, maintaining, and remotely managing instrumentationIdentifying hazardous VOCs in product materials, including compound identification and structural elucidation of VOCs in complex matricesInterpreting data using SAS/JMP statistical approaches and laboratory information management system (LIMS) reporting toolsMaintaining quality-control and quality-assurance practices in compliance with the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)Using data analytics and visualization tools to effectively present analytical findingsFellows are appointed for an initial one-year period, which may be renewed for up to four additional years, for a total fellowship period of up to five years. The starting stipend for a B.S.-level graduate is $4,446.75 per month, plus a monthly supplement for healthinsurance ranging from $692 for individual coverage to $1,467 for family coverage.This fellowship is administered by ORISE. Visit http://orise.orau.gov/cdc for additional information and eligibility requirements. The degree must have been obtained within the past five years. Relocation expenses are not covered. Participants do not become employees of CDC or the program administrator, and no employment-related fringe benefits are provided.QualificationsBachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in chemistry obtained within the past five yearsGrade-point average of 3.5 or higher is desired but not requiredExperience or a strong interest in analytical laboratory workExperience using Agilent GC/MS instruments is desirable but not requiredUndergraduate laboratory research experience is desirable but not requiredA commitment of at least two years is desirable

jobs.title: William M. Lapenta NOAA Student Internship 2027 at National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)
jobs.description: Employer: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Expires: 11/26/2026 OverviewNOAA is offering paid summer internships through the William M. Lapenta NOAA Student Internship Program targeted towards current 2nd and 3rd-year undergraduate and enrolled graduate students to work in areas that will provide robust research and/or operational experience that will prepare the student for further study in NOAA fields, for application to fellowships or for the NOAA-mission workforce. This internship program enables the National Weather Service, (NWS), Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR), National Environmental Satellite Data and Information Service (NESDIS), National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Ocean Service (NOS) and Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO) to target the skills needed to fulfill their specific mission needs. Projects may be focused on research areas or the development of operational products such as decision support tools, climate and weather forecast models, population dynamics of fish populations, ecosystem modeling, hydrology, ocean circulation models, unmanned systems (both in air and under water), data analysis methodologies, social science, and strategies to communicate climate and weather information pertaining to NOAA's mission to the public and to stakeholders. Overall, students will focus on areas that will meet the future needs of NOAA’s ever-broadening user community and address immediate challenges across a diverse spectrum from the sun to the bottom of our oceans.Eligibility: Must be enrolled in an undergraduate (sophomore and junior status only) or graduate degree program (as of during the internship); if not enrolled during the internship intern will be ineligible for Direct Hire. This includes all students graduating before the internship begins. Must be a U.S. Citizen willing to undergo a security background check. US citizenship must be in hand by December 10, 2026.Students from all STEM majors and other majors relevant to NOAA's mission will be considered.How to apply:Application process is conducted via SmartSheets (https://app.smartsheetgov.com/b/form/72e9abb368834d598b275f412d81a9e3) Prepare the following to be uploaded to the site.A personal statementCurriculum Vitae (CV) or resumeA transcript (unofficial is sufficient) from your institutionTwo letters of recommendation are required to be submitted on your behalf. jobs.title: DTRA Kinetic Technology Systems Modeling, Testing and Analysis Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/26/2026 The Test Support Division, Test Science Branch, of the Research and Development Directorate for the Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) is offering a master's/doctoral level fellowship opportunity in kinetic weapons technology. What will I be doing and why should I apply?DTRA-West offers a distinctly unique experience for research-based experiences, professional development, and future career opportunities for selected fellows and interns, not to mention the beauty of Albuquerque and the surrounding area. As a selected candidate, you will engage with researchers and engineers within the DTRA complex and be a part of, and witness to, objective evaluations and assessments of new capabilities aimed at countering WMD and emerging threats. Albuquerque is New Mexico’s largest city, where the modern city skyline is set against a backdrop of the stunning Sandia Mountains and an endless, timeless blue sky. Albuquerque boasts a unique multicultural history and heritage. Native American, Hispanic & Latino cultural influences are a part of everyday life.As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will join and learn from a community of scientists and researchers engaged in planning and accomplishing research projects in the Test Support Division, Test Science Branch at DTRA. You will participate in kinetic and other weapons testing at White Sands Missile Range, Kirtland Air-Force Base, and other test sites.Why should I apply? Under the guidance of a mentor, you will:Learn how to research issues and conduct feasibility studies pertaining to the engineering and scientific elements of prospective projects/testsUnderstand how to design and develop test plans and analysis methodologies through participation in test teamsLearn presentation techniques incorporating information related to kinetic and/or non-kinetic weapons effectsGain experience with diagnostic instrumentation development, gauge ranging, and analyzing test dataLearn how to evaluate test results and document findingsDevelop ability to participate effectively in Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMS) with customers, technical personnel, and contractors to gather technical requirements from all partiesWithin one year, you will gain significant knowledge and experience related to the modeling and analysis of weapons systems interactions with targets and the response and damage of targets to weapons effects. Where will I be located?Albuquerque, New MexicoWhat is the anticipated start date?The Test Support Division, Test Science Branch at DTRA is ready to make appointments immediately. Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and internships or fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified.What is the appointment length?This appointment is a full-time, twelve-month research appointment, with the possibility to be renewed for additional research periods. Appointments may be extended depending on funding availability, project assignment, program rules, and availability of the participant. What are the provisions?You will receive a stipend to be determined by DTRA. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. The anticipated stipend range for this opportunity is $5400-$5800 per month based on full-time participation.Other provisions may include the following:Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE)Relocation/Dislocation AllowanceTraining and Travel AllowanceAbout DTRAThe Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and its allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict. This opportunity is within the Research and Development Directorate of DTRA, Test and Assessment Department. For more information about the DTRA, please visit https://www.dtra.mil/. About ORISEThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and DoD. Participants do not enter into an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DoD or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE. For more information, visit the ORISE Research Participation Program at the U.S. Department of Defense.

jobs.title: Student Trainee (Energy Industry Analysis) at Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Expires: 11/27/2026 SummaryThe Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) is ranked within the top 5 mid-size agencies as a "Best Place to Work" in the Federal government! Our Pathways Internship Program provides students the opportunity to acquire first-hand experience in the energy industry, while gaining exposure to the Commission's work. This Student Trainee (Energy Industry Analysis) vacancy will be used to fill multiple intern positions in OAL, OEMR, OERA, OPP, OTRE and the Office of Commissioner Rosner. DutiesHelp This vacancy is for a Spring/Summer 2027 internship.While the duties of the Student Trainee (Energy Industry Analysis) may vary depending on office placement, some of your typical work assignments may include:In the Office of Administrative Litigation (OAL): Student Trainee (EIAs) assist analysts with the review, summary, and analysis of data to use in the settlement and litigation of cases before Administrative Law Judges at the Commission. This assistance may include preparing spreadsheets to summarize cost, volume, or economic data, managing discovery responses, researching precedent, reading testimony, and attending settlement conferences and hearings.In the Office of Energy Market Regulation (OEMR): Assisting professional staff members in performing analyses of economic and regulatory issues associated with filings for the purpose of identifying trends, problems, or deviations from pertinent regulatory requirements or Commission policies and developing recommendations to resolve issues for use by the team leader or supervisor.In the Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting (OERA): Student Trainee (EIAs) assist in the analysis of electric and gas markets, assessing market fundamentals and trends, as well as complex issues related to market structure, conduct, and performance. Trainees analyze and develop large volumes of data using Python, SQL, R, Databricks, Posit, PowerBI, and/or CoPilot, working independently to summarize anomalous market outcomes and visually present data. A trainee more focused on data engineering may support enhancing data workflows, streamlining operational processes, and improving analytical efficiency by developing data pipelines, automation tools, ETL workflows, cloud based analytics infrastructure, and other technical components that enable OERA's analytical functions.In the Office of Technical Reporting and Economics (OTRE): Assisting professional staff in analyzing energy markets, energy infrastructure, and factors affecting the reliability and operation of the electric and natural gas systems. May involve some or all of the following: reviewing and analyzing industry reports, energy market data, and regulatory filings to identify trends and emerging issues; supporting the preparation of technical reports, presentations, and briefing materials to inform the Commission's work; and managing large datasets and conducting quantitative and economic analyses using statistical software and other analytical tools.In the Office of Commissioner David Rosner: Student Trainees assist with the review, summary, and analysis of substantive matters within the Commission's jurisdiction. This assistance may include preparation of memos on legal and/or technical issues arising under the Federal Power Act, Natural Gas Act, and the Interstate Commerce Act; background research for the Commissioner's public statements and engagements; participation in meetings with external stakeholders; and completion of other projects as assigned.The intern program at FERC is unique in that we post one intern vacancy for multiple offices to make selections. This means you may be contacted by several different hiring managers for different vacancies. See Next Steps section for additional information.Our Internship Program offers students the opportunity to attend networking events, visit regulated hydropower dams, and participate in seminars with career advice and tips from FERC's top management officials. For more information, visit: https://www.ferc.gov/about/careers/student-relations.

jobs.title: 2027 METx Data & Analytics Intern at MetLife
jobs.description: Employer: MetLife - Global Technology and Operations Expires: 11/30/2026 The Team You Will JoinAt MetLife, data isn’t just a tool – it is a catalyst for growth. As part of our Data & Analytics organization, you’ll unlock trusted insights that drive bold decisions, power personalized customer experiences, and deliver lasting business impact. We’re building the future of data – one that’s governed responsibly, engineered for scalability, and designed for growth. When you join us, you’re not just supporting the business – you’re empowering it. Let’s transform insight into impact and data into action, together. The OpportunityAs a METx Data & Analytics undergraduate intern, you’ll work alongside experienced data professionals, contribute to real projects, and share your outcomes and learning experiences with peers and leaders at the end of the program. Our program is designed for students who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn new technologies in a collaborative, innovative environment. Application Process & Program InformationApplications for this role will close December 1, 2026.Qualified candidates will be invited to interview on a rolling basis – no interview activity will take place between December 21, 2026 through January 18, 2027.Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and must not require MetLife sponsorship or support for a work permit or visa in any capacity now or in the future.Interns will start in person on June 1st, 2027 and will work approximately 40 hours /week over the course of ten weeks – candidates must be available for the entire duration of the program.All D&A interns will be hybrid in Cary, NC.MetLife does not provide housing or a relocation/housing stipend or support for this role. Key ResponsibilitiesOur interns work on meaningful projects impacting millions of customers, receive mentorship from highly skilled data experts and industry leaders, and build robust technical skills. Intern projects may include: Data Engineering & Pipeline Automation: Automate data pipelines using Azure and Databricks to support business reporting.Machine Learning & Predictive Analytics: Develop machine learning models to predict customer behavior, pricing, threat monitoring, and other outcomes based on historical data patterns.Generative AI & Agentic AI Innovation: Brainstorm and develop potential GenAI and Agentic AI solutions to enhance operations and capabilities.Analytics Solution Development: Develop and test analytics solutions, including writing Databricks notebooks and validating data.Business Process Analysis & Improvement: Analyze, identify opportunities for improvement, and document business processes to support data-driven projects.Data Visualization & Reporting: Build dashboards and reports to visualize key business metrics.Production Support & Incident Management: Provide production support and help resolve data-related incidents.Data Governance & Management: Document key data assets, apply data governance standards, and support data management to improve transparency and compliance.Strategic Initiatives & Cross-Functional Collaboration: Support strategic or operational initiatives while collaborating with cross-functional teams. Required QualificationsCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s degree or post-secondary training in Data Science, Business Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Management Information Systems, or a related field.Must have an expected graduation date no later than June 2029.Minimum GPA of 3.0.Strong analytical mindset with ability to identify patterns and insights from data as demonstrated through academic coursework or personal projects.Coursework or experience with at least one programming language or analytics tool (e.g., Python, SQL, Scala, C#, C++).Ability to analyze, ingest, and organize raw data and perform data transformation for modeling.Knowledge of or experience using AI models, integrating AI-enabled solutions into business or technical workflows.Desire to learn new technologies, tools, and business processes.Strong communication and critical thinking, and teamwork skills.Curiosity, adaptability, and a growth mindset. Preferred QualificationsExposure to data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) or cloud platforms.Familiarity with cloud-based data and analytics environments, particularly Microsoft Azure and Databricks.Experience with collaborative tools (e.g., GitHub, Azure DevOps) or agile methodologies.Exposure to data governance tools (e.g., Collibra, Ataccama, EDC).Relevant certifications (e.g., Microsoft Certified: Data Analyst Associate).Experience with data pipelines, systems, and process design.Exposure to advanced analytics, machine learning, and feature engineering. Location Expectation: This is a hybrid role requiring a minimum of 3 days per week in office. The expected salary range for this position is $28-30 /Hour. About MetLife Recognized on Fortune magazine's list of the "World's Most Admired Companies", Fortune World’s 25 Best Workplaces™, as well as the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For®, MetLife, through its subsidiaries and affiliates, is one of the world’s leading financial services companies; providing insurance, annuities, employee benefits and asset management to individual and institutional customers. With operations in more than 40 markets, we hold leading positions in the United States, Latin America, Asia, Europe, and the Middle East. As part of our New Frontier strategy, MetLife is building an AI-enabled, people-centered future. We’re looking for people who bring curiosity, adaptability, and a growth mindset as we use AI to enhance how we serve customers, support communities, and evolve the way work gets done. At MetLife, AI is a responsible partner that supports human judgment, creativity, and continuous improvement while helping us build trust, inclusion, and long-term value. Our purpose is simple - to help our colleagues, customers, communities, and the world at large create a more confident future. United by purpose and guided by our core values - Win Together, Do the Right Thing, Deliver Impact Over Activity, and Think Ahead - we’re inspired to transform the next century in financial services. At MetLife, it’s #AllTogetherPossible. Join us!

jobs.title: Regulatory Veterinary Summer Internship Program at Ohio Department of Agriculture
jobs.description: Employer: Ohio Department of Agriculture - Animal Health Expires: 12/01/2026 PDF Applications Due January 1, 2027 - Contact HR@agri.ohio.gov for detailsThis is a 10-week PAID summer internship hosted at the Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA) for a current veterinary student that is interested in working in regulatory medicine. This internship is designed to prepare veterinary students for a career in regulatory/government medicine as well as to bring awareness of the different jobs and career paths that a veterinarian could have working for ODA. Being a regulatory veterinarian requires a unique skill set that is often hard to address in the classroom curriculum. This program is an opportunity to gain hands on experience within the Department of Agriculture.During the ten weeks, you will spend time in 4 sections of ODA:The Division of Animal Health Field Operations: Assist our field veterinarians and inspectors as they participate in county fair compliance checks, livestock care standards visits, TB testing, sale barn visits, Captive Deer Farm inspections, and foreign animal disease (FAD) investigations.The Division of Meat Inspection Field Operations: Ride along with our field veterinarians as they conduct humane handling visits, routine slaughter operation evaluations, carcass dispositions, and compliance visits at state inspected slaughter facilities.The Division of Animal Health Administration: Shadow the Emergency Coordinator, Assistant State Veterinarian, and other administrators as they participate in daily work unit meetings and task forces on a variety of topics from foreign animal disease to emergency response. Assist with health paper documentation and epidemiologic questionnaires.Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory. Spend time in all sections of our laboratory: virology, pathology, bacteriology, molecular diagnostics, and avian serology. Learn how the different tests are conducted and the importance of these tests to our industry.The end of the summer internship culminates in a presentation to ODA staff.

jobs.title: EPA Development and Qualification of In Vitro Blood-Brain Barrier Models for Environmental Chemical Screening at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/03/2026 Application Deadline12/18/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription*Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.EPA Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP), located in Durham, North Carolina.The mission of EPA is to protect human health and the environment. EPA works to ensure that: Americans have clean air, land and water; National efforts to reduce environmental risks are based on the best available scientific information; Federal laws protecting human health and the environment are administered and enforced fairly, effectively and as Congress intended; Environmental stewardship is integral to U.S. policies concerning natural resources, human health, economic growth, energy, transportation, agriculture, industry, and international trade, and these factors are similarly considered in establishing environmental policy; All parts of society have access to accurate information sufficient to effectively participate in managing human health and environmental risks; Contaminated lands and toxic sites are cleaned up; and chemicals in the marketplace are reviewed for safety.Research Project: The Risk Assessment Support Division (RASD) within the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s (US EPA) Office of Mission Critical Operations (OMCO) of the Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP) supports Agency decisions by providing solutions-driven research to rapidly evaluate the risks associated with environmental chemical exposures. A key component of this work is the application of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) including in vitro, in chemico, and in silico approaches to generate human relevant information for chemical hazard and risk assessment. These approaches support Agency's commitment to reduce or replace vertebrate animal testing while providing accurate and reliable data to safeguard human health and the environment. RASD develops and applies physiologically relevant in vitro models, high-throughput screening assays, and computational and informatics approaches to advance predictive, human-relevant toxicological assessment. As part of our in vitro NAM development, we are actively seeking a research participant to join our team and learn about the advancement of in vitro blood-brain barrier (BBB) models. You will gain experience with the establishment and optimization of in vitro BBB model systems, chemical exposure assays, and permeability and transport studies. Data generated through these studies will be used to inform in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation and support the development, parameterization, calibration, and evaluation of physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models of chemical disposition and brain exposure. The overall goal is to improve predictions of chemical brain exposure and distribution while advancing human-relevant approaches for chemical safety assessment. To bridge this gap, EPA’s Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention is pioneering in vitro 'New Approach Method' (NAM) testing strategies to enable fast, cost-effective screening, prioritization, and human health risk assessments. This specific internship is deeply anchored within the analytical chemistry foundation necessary to validate and drive these alternative strategies forward.As an intern on our team, you will gain experience with EPA’s Risk Assessment Support Division by learning about analytical chemistry method development, validation, and execution. Your primary learning objective will be designing robust sample preparation and quantitative analysis procedures to track chemical concentrations and stability within complex in vitro and biochemical assay matrices, specifically targeted at biological perturbations such as endocrine disruption.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will learn to operate and troubleshoot advanced instrumentation, utilizing high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) and liquid/gas chromatography (LC-MS/MS, GC-MS/MS) to generate high-quality, reproducible kinetic profiles. By pairing your rigorous analytical measurements with exposure-dose and toxicokinetic modeling, you will directly enable the team to translate laboratory data into 'equivalent doses,' allowing scientists to compare systemic configurations against anticipated exposure levels to evaluate overall risk (hazard + exposure = risk).Learning objectives include:Advanced Method Development & Validation: Gain hands-on experience in designing, optimizing, and validating highly sensitive, selective analytical chemistry methods to extract and quantify trace-level organic chemicals across diverse and challenging biological and cell-culture matrices.High-Throughput Analytical Instrumentation: Master the operation, calibration, and troubleshooting of advanced instrumentation, including ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple-quadrupole and high-resolution mass spectrometers (UHPLC-MS/MS, Q-TOF).In Vitro Toxicokinetics (IVTK) Characterization: Develop proficiency in calculating chemical parameters, including hepatic metabolic clearance rates, plasma/media protein binding, and chemical stability, which are vital for determining points of departure for endocrine disruption pathways.Data Analysis Automation & Quality Assurance: Learn to implement automated data processing pipelines for mass spectrometry datasets, apply rigorous QA/QC metrics, and maintain strict data integrity practices matching good laboratory practices (GLP).Regulatory Integration & Cross-Disciplinary Teamwork: Understand how raw analytical chemistry data directly translates through exposure models to shape EPA screening, prioritization, and toxicological policy decisions, while enhancing collaborative communication across chemical and biological domains.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Deon Moore (moore.deon@epa.gov). jobs.title: Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) - Gaithersburg, MD at National Institute of Standards and Technology
jobs.description: Employer: National Institute of Standards and Technology Expires: 12/03/2026 The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) seeks undergraduate students for the Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) program. This vacancy announcement is for in-person fellowships in Gaithersburg, MD. An additional vacancy announcement is open for in-person fellowships in Boulder, CO (vacancy #SURF-2027-0002). Applicants may apply to both vacancies and use the same documents for all applications. Learn more at https://www.nist.gov/surf.Clarification from the agency:Current full-time undergraduate (first-year, sophomore, junior, or senior) degree-seeking students enrolled at accredited 2-year or 4-year colleges or universities in the U.S. or U.S. territories. Note: First-year and graduating seniors (defined as seniors participating in the Summer, Winter or Spring Commencement) are encouraged to apply to the program.Duties:The SURF program provides research opportunities for students to work with internationally known NIST scientists and engineers, to expose them to cutting-edge research and promote the pursuit of advanced degrees and careers in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). SURF gives students an opportunity to:Gain substantive career experience related to academic interestsAcquire lifelong leadership, management, and analytical skillsLearn about a career in public serviceBuild professional relationships, contacts, and networksObserve the daily operations and working environment of a premier federal laboratoryImagine Yourself in the NIST LaboratoriesNIST welcomes students from a broad range of STEM disciplines, including but not limited to biochemistry, biology, biophysics, chemistry, computer science, engineering, materials science, mathematics, nanoscale science, neutron research, physics, and statistics. Students work under the guidance of a research mentor in one of the participating laboratories or program offices. The following laboratories and offices participate in the SURF Gaithersburg program: Communications Technology Laboratory (CTL)Engineering Laboratory (EL)Information Technology Laboratory (ITL)Material Measurement Laboratory (MML) in partnership with the NIST Center for Neutron Research (NCNR)Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML)Other offices occasionally host SURF participants: Office of Advanced Manufacturing (OAM), Communications and Outreach Office (COO), Research Data and Computing Office (RDCO), Technology Partnerships Office (TPO), Standards Coordination Office (SCO)As part of the application process, all applicants must identify and select first and second-choice host laboratories/offices for placement consideration. Applicants should carefully choose host laboratories/offices because the completed application is considered primarily by the first-choice host laboratory. Due to the multidisciplinary nature of NIST's research, we encourage students to look through the different laboratory websites to discover interesting project areas. For example, a computer science student may find project opportunities in CTL, PML, and EL in addition to the logical choice of ITL. Similar opportunities exist for those in other disciplines. For a detailed description of SURF projects in each NIST laboratory and prior acceptance rates, students are encouraged to review laboratory descriptions and acceptance rates at https://www.nist.gov/surf/surf-gaithersburg/research-programs. All students must work at the NIST campus in Gaithersburg, MD for the entire appointment.While duties and responsibilities may vary by laboratory, all students must:Attend OrientationWork with their mentor on a designated research projectAttend the SURF seminar seriesCompose and submit an abstract halfway through the program summarizing research accomplishmentsDeliver an oral presentation during the final week of the program

jobs.title: Regenerative Farm Internship at Deck Family Farm
jobs.description: Employer: Deck Family Farm Expires: 12/03/2026 LEARN TO RUN A PROFITABLE FARM BUSINESSDeck Family Farm Education Program's mission is to train the next generation of farmers in building successful agricultural careers. Our year-round program teaches you how to operate a diversified, profitable farm enterprise—balancing consumer demand for quality products with sound business practices and environmental stewardship.This is hands-on business education. Second and third-year students advance to management positions with increased responsibility and leadership roles. This program builds the skillset to launch your own operation or manage large-scale agricultural businesses.Certifications & Standards: Certified Organic (Oregon Tilth), AGA Certified, GAP Humane Handling, Salmon Safe. Modest accommodations (shared housing, cabin, or adobe house). Externship opportunities and research project support available. Farm Enterprises are as follows:Raw milk dairy: Milking an average of 16-18 cows year round. The herd is held as a cooperative and owned by shareholders who pay for feed, care and milking of the herd. Butter, cheese, and yogurt along with fresh milk are produced for shareholders.Heritage pasture-raised hazelnut-finished pork. Sows farrow in the barn in the winter. Piglets are fed raw milk from the dairy during weaning and finished on hazelnuts. We produce our pigs birth to finish.100% Grass fed and finished Certified Organic Heritage Galloway beef. Management intensive grazing has brought greater fertility to farm pastures, and rotating crops of grains, legumes and grasses has extended our grazing season to 8-9 months of the year.Poultry : Certified Organic heritage layers for eggs, and roasters for meat. All chickens are out on pasture during the day and housed in chicken trailers or tractors at night to prevent predation. Chickens are grazed behind and beside cattle. Much of our grazing for the sheep flock is on leased organic, off-site ground.Vegetables: Graziers Garden provides veggies for the Full Farm CSA (FFCSA) which is housed at the farm and supplies CSA members with meat, milk, eggs, veg, fruit, nuts, grains, ferments, and more.Marketing: Students participate in all aspects of farm sales including CSA (Community Supported Agriculture) program, farmers markets, wholesale accounts, warehousing and financial analysis. jobs.description: Employer: Pocono Springs Camp Expires: 12/04/2026 Have you always wanted to work with kids and develop your teaching skills?! We're looking for Nature Counselors!Experience the most rewarding summer of your life! Work and make friends with 100+ people from around the world AND have the opportunity to inspire kids every single day! At Pocono Springs, prepare yourself to get outdoors and step away from technology as you build real-life skills relatable to any future career ambitions! Who we're looking for:We're looking for responsible, enthusiastic, and spirited individuals who can serve as role models, mentors, and teachers at camp for summer 2027. About the role:The Pocono Springs Camp experience is 7 weeks long, with 2 weeks of orientation and 5 weeks of traditional summer camp.Get the opportunity to contribute to making incredible memories, all while having the summer of a lifetime! We pride ourselves on our staff satisfaction. We welcome all feedback and make it a priority to provide support to our counselors, as well as a platform for you to bring your passion and creativity to camp! jobs.description: Employer: NeuroSync Expires: 12/04/2026 Job DescriptionSummer Data Scientist Intern - NeuroSync, Inc.📍 Location: Holliston, MA → In-Person⏳ Duration: Spring 2027 ( Full time) 💰 Compensation: Paid InternshipAbout the Role:We are seeking a Data Scientist Intern to support business operations and strategy through data-driven insights during Spring 2027. In this role, you will work on forecasting models, analyze market and operational trends, and help identify new business opportunities. This is a hands-on opportunity to apply machine learning, statistical modeling, and business analytics to real-world challenges.Key Responsibilities:Develop forecasting models to predict market trends, operational efficiency, and business performance.Analyze large datasets to identify patterns, trends, and key business opportunities.Provide data-driven recommendations to improve operations, sales, and customer engagement.Support financial and operational analysis through advanced data modeling techniques.Build interactive dashboards and visualizations to communicate key insights to stakeholders.Leverage predictive analytics to optimize decision-making in business operations.Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive strategic growth initiatives.Work with SQL, Python, or R to process, clean, and analyze complex business datasets.Conduct A/B testing and scenario analysis to evaluate business strategies.Required Skills & Qualifications:✅ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Data Science, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related field.✅ Strong programming skills in Python, R, or SQL for data manipulation and analysis.✅ Experience with forecasting models, trend analysis, and business intelligence.✅ Familiarity with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Salesforce).✅ Knowledge of machine learning algorithms and predictive analytics.✅ Understanding of business operations, financial modeling, and market analysis.✅ Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills with a business-oriented mindset.✅ Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) or big data tools (Hadoop, Spark) is a plus.What You’ll Gain:Real-world experience in using data science to drive business decisions.The opportunity to work with large-scale datasets in an operational setting.Exposure to forecasting, financial analysis, and strategic business modeling.Mentorship and networking with business leaders and data professionals.

jobs.title: Grad Intern – Biostatistics at Amgen
jobs.description: Employer: Amgen Expires: 12/04/2026 Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving PatientsAt Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.Grad Intern – Biostatistics (Summer 2027)What You Will DoLet’s do this. Let’s change the world. Amgen’s 10 – 13-week internship program offers meaningful project experiences that impact patient’s lives. This internship provides the opportunity for executive and social networking events and to participate in community volunteer projects while providing competitive compensation. Limited relocation housing and/or transportation allowance may be available for eligible candidates.This position will work closely with a senior-level statistician on topics related to the design and analysis of clinical trials and/or nonclinical research.Amgen research and development uses science and innovation to dramatically improve people’s lives in various therapeutic areas, including oncology, nephrology, bone metabolism, cardiovascular, and inflammation.At the conclusion of the internship, this position will give a presentation summarizing the work completed during the program.Program Eligibility RequirementsMust be available to work a full-time schedule.Expected continued enrollment in an accredited college or university following the internship program / co-opStudent must be located in the United States for the duration of the internship programWhat We Expect of YouWe are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The collaborative individual we seek is a team-player with these qualifications:Basic Qualifications:Amgen requires that all individuals applying for a grad internship or a co-op assignment at Amgen must meet the following criteria:18 years or olderGraduated with a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or universityCurrently enrolled in an MBA program for an MBA internship OR a Master’s program for a Master’s internship OR a PharmD program for a PharmD internship OR Ph.D. for a PhD internship from an accredited college or university and completion of the first year of MBA OR Master’s OR Pharm D OR Ph.D. program before the internship startsPreferred Qualifications:Pursuing a PhD in Biostatistics, Statistics, or MathematicsIn the process of completing the third year of current programProficiency in SAS or R on either a UNIX or NT platformAbility to lead and deliver results in an interactive matrixed environmentStrong written and oral communication skills, relationship building, and leadership skillWhat You Can Expect of UsAs we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.The base pay range for this opportunity in the U.S. is $35.34 – $41.20 per hour.Build a network of colleagues that will endure and grow throughout your time with us and beyond.Bring your authentic self to the table and become the professional you’re inspired to be through accepting a culture that values the diversity of thought and experience and will flex to your strengths and possibilities.Participate in executive and social networking events, as well as community volunteer projects.Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team.careers.amgen.com - Please search for Keyword R-259820In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.Application deadlineAmgen does not have an application deadline for this position; we will continue accepting applications until we receive a sufficient number or select a candidate for the position.SponsorshipCandidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. for the duration of this program. Sponsorship for future FTE roles is not guaranteed.As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of diverse, ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease.Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other basis protected by applicable law.We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

jobs.title: Data Analyst Intern at South Bend Community School Corporation
jobs.description: Employer: South Bend Community School Corporation Expires: 12/04/2026 Duration: 3 – 6 MonthsDepartment: Data, Technology & System Improvement Role OverviewWe are looking for a sharp, detail-oriented Data Analyst Intern to join our team. You will be deep in the syntax of R to strengthen the district’s data infrastructure and transform messy raw data into actionable insights. Under the supervision of the Director of Data and Reporting, you will clean complex datasets, perform data analysis, and build processes to maintain data integrity. Position Type:Full-TimeSalary:$20 to $20 Per Hour

jobs.title: COLLEGE CO-OP MSD/COMPLIANCE SERVICES DIVISION (LABORATORY) at City of Cincinnati
jobs.description: Employer: City of Cincinnati Expires: 12/05/2026 MSD DIVISION OF COMPLIANCE SERVICES - LABORATORY Mission: To establish a partnership with colleges and universities, exposing as many students as possible to employment opportunities in the Wastewater Industry and help them become experienced professionals in the next generation workforce.Purpose: To attract and cultivate bright and energetic college students and maintain ongoing partnerships with colleges and universities. It is our goal to expose these students to applied laboratory practices, as well as career opportunities in water resource management and the environmental sciences. The Co-op program also serves as a recruitment tool to assist the Compliance Services Division (CSD), Laboratory section in hiring full-time personnel. Overview: The co-op student will be assigned to specific areas of the laboratory to participate in wet weather projects, special studies, and/or daily routine testing. Under the supervision of a chemist, co-ops will be exposed to various tasks performed in the laboratory and on the analytical equipment utilized. The CSD Laboratory program strives to reinforce the knowledge and skills the students have learned in the classroom and to build on those skills in a setting that provides "hands-on" instruction and experience.Expectations: The Co-op students will be assigned to the Nutrient, Metals, and Sample Check-in Units where they will be trained in analyzing treatment plant NPDES permit samples, process control, wet weather, industrial waste, and/or special studies samples. They will be trained to perform a variety of analyses which may include sample receiving process, ammonia, nitrite and nitrate, total phosphorus, total orthophosphate, total Kjeldahl nitrogen, biochemical oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, alkalinity, total hardness, and suspended, total and dissolved solids. They will also be trained in running bacteriological samples for fecal coliform and E. coli analysis. Many of these procedures will involve the use of analytical equipment. They will learn the proper Quality Control to be run in analyzing these samples. They will also be trained in using the LIMS data entry program.Learning Milestones: Lab/Project orientation (week 1)Pertinent instruction for equipment or methodologies employed (week 1-4)Periodic status report (week 5-11)Completion of project/report out (week 12)All studies have been previously designed, and each student will be assigned to a specific study as his/her primary project.If the student has done a previous term at MSD, the project will be a continuation of that work.In addition to their primary project, students will be expected to perform other laboratory tasks and help in other areas as assistance is needed.The CSD lab attempts to expose students to all facets of laboratory analysis during the term. **Co-Ops may be required to work Tuesday-Saturday, day shift** HR Contact: Jerrold Ware, Jerrold.Ware@cincinnati-oh.gov

jobs.title: Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator at Polk County Conservation
jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 12/05/2026 The Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator plays a vital role in advocating for and enhancing outdoor recreation opportunities within Polk County Conservation. This position focuses on expanding Veteran’s programming, youth mental health initiatives, and enhancing current Equestrian Center program offerings. AmeriCorps Volunteers serving with the Equestrian Center will have dual enrollment in the Youth Mental Health Corps (YMHC) that is a nationwide initiative. Participants gain valuable practical skills through professional trainings and certification programs. The YMHC program is limited to individuals who are between the ages of 18-24; persons outside of that age range are ineligible for enrollment. This position is supportive and preventative in nature, not clinical. Volunteers do not provide therapy, counseling, diagnoses, or independent crisis intervention, nor are they expected to manage mental health emergencies beyond their training and comfortability. Instead, they help connect youth with appropriate staff and resources while contributing to a supportive outdoor environment. Through this service, Volunteers advance Polk County Conservation’s mission by making outdoor recreation and conservation education more accessible and meaningful for local youth, while helping foster the development of social connections and supportive experiences that contribute to the well-being of Polk County residents. One Quarter-Time Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($6,270) paid equally over the course of 450 hours of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon successful completion ($1,956.35) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. This position is Quarter-Time; Volunteers will serve a minimum of 450 hours over the course of 32 weeks, serving a minimum of 10 hours/week from January to May and a minimum of 24 hours/week from June to August. This posting is not a direct position of Polk County Conservation, and successful applicants will not be employees of Polk County. Successful applicants will not be subject to terms and conditions of Polk County employment and will not be eligible for any employee benefits provided by Polk County. However, these positions will be serving with Polk County Conservation, a host site of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program, and will be subject to AmeriCorps rules, benefits, and federal requirements. Volunteer Schedule January to May January program orientation and YMHC trainings Volunteer will spend a minimum of 10 hours/week participating in position-specific orientation and trainings. Some elements of the orientation and training can be completed via teleservice, but requires prior approval from Program Coordinator February program sessions begin: Monday evenings 4pm-8pm; Volunteer will complete YMHC tasks to meet the minimum of 10 hours/week June to August Summer youth programming sessions begin: Monday-Thursday 7am-2pm; 24 hours/week A 30-minute meal break will be allocated to the volunteer if they serve five consecutive hours in one service day; these 30 minutes cannot be counted towards the required 450 service hours Every service day will include one 15-minute break; additional breaks must be taken if the temperature is above 85 degrees Volunteer may serve during special events that take place on some weekends A minimum of two weeks’ notice will be given to Volunteer prior to the event occurring Volunteer will be allowed to flex hours during the week if there is an event occurring over the weekend to promote a healthy workload * Volunteers must not serve any hours on the major federal holidays – New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day. This includes checking emails, self-directed training, or teleservice. If the Host Site is open on one of these holidays and volunteers are expected to serve, the site supervisor should work with Program to gain approval for this volunteer service prior to the holiday. For any of the other federal holidays, including MLK Day, Presidents Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans Day, Host Sites will communicate expectations of volunteer service in advance. If the Host Site is closed on one of more of those lesser holidays (including the day after Thanksgiving or Christmas eve) or the Host Site recognizes other workdays when major federal holidays fall on weekend days, volunteers should not check their email, complete timesheets, or do teleservice on those days either unless they follow the procedure above. Sick or personal leave, and holidays is allowed, but such time off does not count towards the required number of hours needed to successfully complete the term of service. There are additional benefits offered if the volunteer has a compelling personal circumstance. The Quarter-Time Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator will receive two weeks of comprehensive training focused on the Jester Park Equestrian Center. Volunteers will become familiar with the facility, current equine services offered, current public outreach efforts, basic equine husbandry, fundamentals of speech to communicate with program attendees, and basics of program development. Volunteers will continue to receive on-the-job training outside of the first two weeks to improve their understanding of the changing needs of the public demographic that utilizes the Jester Park Equestrian Center. All participants in the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Youth Mental Health Corps Program that serve around youth or vulnerable adults are required to complete the following trainings: CPR/AED and first aid certification through the American Heart Association via online modules and an in-person practical skills test Mental Health First Aid Iowa DHS Mandatory Reporter Training ACEs 360 Volunteers may select between two YMHC workforce pathways based on their personal career goals. Community Health Worker: Public health for community health workers training (12 hours total) - required Youth mental health foundations training (2 hours total) - required School-based Mental Health Navigator: Volunteers enrolled in this pathway must select a minimum of one of the listed programs to meet the minimum requirements. Direct support professional behavioral and mental health certificate through DMACC (54 hours total) Registered behavioral technician certificate through University of Kansas (40 hours total) Requires additional registration for exam and passing of exam to receive certificate Paraeducator certification program (90 hours total) Additional Optional Trainings: Motivational Interviewing (2 hours total) School Mental Health Training through University of Iowa (multiple module options to choose from) Iowa Area Education Agencies (catalogue of additional trainings) Community Health Worker Specialization Trainings – must complete initial community health worker trainings Maternal Health Training (6 hours total) Mental Health Training (4.5 hours) Essential Functions: Develop and facilitate deliverable mental health programming that centers around outdoor recreation and the outdoors – primary audience of individuals between the ages of 13-24 Volunteers may also create handouts, infographics, social media videos, blog posts, or other forms of public resources for education and advocacy of mental health topics Volunteers will receive access to Canva for the creation of deliverables as well as a Google account for the development of program offerings All public deliverables must be approved by the Polk County Conservation Community Outreach staff before it can be utilized with Polk County residents Provide knowledgeable support to Polk County Conservation staff when navigating behavior management of program participants The Volunteer will utilize the information and skills developed from the training they complete and will provide appropriate resources to program participants as needed Establish a resource list that can be distributed to Polk County staff, community members, and other local organizations Design and facilitate a minimum of one equine-assisted service tailored to the needs and interests of Veterans and youth demographics during service term The volunteer-developed program will be focused on improving the emotional regulation and well-being of community members through the use of horses Facilitate and manage professional connections with Veteran service organizations and healthcare providers in the Polk County area to identify community members who could benefit from equine-assisted services and outdoor recreation opportunities The volunteer is responsible for communicating with partner organizations via email and phone about program opportunities to share with persons that utilize respective services The volunteer is responsible for promoting the program opportunity to partner organizations and prospective partner organizations to increase the number of individuals that the program positively impacts Assist with the promotion of the program by collecting photos of consenting program participants during programming to utilize for social media posts and for use on the Jester Park Equestrian Center website Work closely with full-time Equestrian Staff to develop, enhance, and diversify program offerings by incorporating new activities, therapeutic riding opportunities, and community outreach initiatives to better serve the needs and interests of the community Educate program participants on the physical and mental health benefits of equine-assisted activities and the therapeutic value of outdoor recreation Monitor program participant progress and outcomes through ongoing assessment and evaluation of program effectiveness through participant check-ins and surveys Non-Essential Functions: Engage in professional development opportunities to enhance knowledge and skills related to the environment, mental health, or youth management Record and maintain data such as number of program participants, type of program offered, location, average age of individuals, activity completed, etc. Conduct public surveys to determine how to effectively support Polk County residents when it comes to navigating mental health challenges and biases Volunteers may engage in other allowable activities that are not specifically outlined in the position description but that support the AmeriCorps program design and that will help the Program meet its goals. Under no circumstances will volunteers be asked to perform prohibited activities. Desired Skills/Qualifications: In pursuit of a Bachelor’s degree in psychology, human services, education, environmental science, outdoor recreation, or other related field AND/OR interest in providing support for community members navigating mental health challenges Comfortable working around horses of varying sizes and basic knowledge of equine-based recreation Experience working with children Passion for utilizing outdoor recreation for the purposes of improving mental health in a non-clinical format Knowledge or awareness of present-day mental health challenges Comfortability with public speaking and presenting programming independently Effective communication and interpersonal skills Eligibility Criteria: Be between the ages of 18 to 24 during the duration of the service term; persons outside of this age range are ineligible for the position at this time Pass a national service criminal history check prior to first day of service Hold one of the following citizenship statuses: US citizen, US national, or lawful permanent resident Possess a valid driver’s license and previous driving experience: Candidate must be comfortable with driving on all road types (gravel, grass, highways, rural, and city roads) Candidate must be comfortable driving in any environmental conditions (daytime, nighttime, rain, fog, sleet, ice, and snow) Candidate must be willing to drive to any location within Polk County, Iowa Candidate must pass a motor vehicle record check before they can operate any county vehicle Candidates with limited driving experience may be considered on a case-by-case basis Benefits: Education Award received upon successful completion of their term of service. Living Allowance Childcare coverage if the volunteer qualifies Housing opportunities provided by Polk County Conservation upon request Student loan forbearance and interest payments for eligible loans Certification in CPR/AED and first aid Mental Health First Aid Training Iowa DHS Mandatory Reporter Training ACEs 360 Training Performance Evaluation & Reporting Requirements: Volunteer Performance Evaluation requirements during the term Regular bi-weekly submission of volunteer timesheets Regular weekly submission of project data from each task a volunteer works on Daily progress reports to Polk County Conservation staff

Applicants who propose topics focused on the history of research in women’s health will automatically be considered for both positions.Project DescriptionAs part of the submission, the applicant will propose a research project centered on a topic of historical importance related to NIH’s contributions to biomedical knowledge and practice. Scholars selected for this opportunity will receive mentorship from at least one biomedical researcher in a relevant NIH ICO as well as from ONHM’s professional historians. Project proposals should be designed to take full advantage of this unique dual-learning opportunity to combine historical research and an enhanced understanding of scientific inquiry to foster a deeper, richer appreciation of the NIH's impact on science, medicine, and society. To learn more about ONHM and its historical resources, visit https://history.nih.gov/ or email us at history@nih.gov.What will I be doing?As an ONHM Stetten Scholar, you will learn to:Understand and Articulate the Historical Significance of NIH Research:Scholars will enhance their ability to analyze and explain the historical importance of a specified area of research initiated, conducted, or overseen by NIH. Projects should include an examination of how NIH research has addressed public, scientific, or governmental concerns over time, in part by identifying new questions, changes, or challenges that emerged as a result of its findings.Effectively Communicate Scientific and Historical Concepts to a General Audience:Scholars will master clearly and effectively explaining core scientific, clinical, and/or technical aspects of historically important developments rooted at NIH, especially in addressing audiences without specialized knowledge. This skill includes addressing outcomes such as new and unresolved scientific and technical questions, surprising findings, social and ethical considerations, or major shifts in standards, metrics, methodologies, or expectations. The goal is to make complex historical and scientific insights accessible and engaging for non-specialists.Present Historically and Scientifically Sound Insights to STEM Audiences:Fellows will refine their ability to communicate significant, historically accurate insights about NIH research to sophisticated STEM audiences. Specifically, they will learn to present historical findings in a way that resonates with established professionals and advanced trainees in fields in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics by ensuring sound, compelling integration of historical context and scientific rigor. The goal is to make historical context and considerations clear, engaging, and accessible to subject-matter experts in related scientific and technical fields.Why should I apply?Under the guidance of mentors in both historical research and relevant biomedical specialties, you will have the opportunity to develop your research skills as an historian; engage with active scientific and clinical researchers; and gain direct exposure to advanced intellectual techniques, tools, and technologies. This opportunity provides a platform to work with scientific and clinical experts as well as professional historians; enhance your ability to connect with broader audiences regarding biomedical topics; and provide an educational, real-world experience that can enhance your career path.Visit ONHM’s website at https://history.nih.gov/ or email the staff at history@nih.gov to explore the historical resources related to your research interests.Where will I be located?Bethesda, MarylandWhat are the provisions?Participants will receive:A $71,000 stipend, paid monthly, as determined by the Office of NIH History & Stetten Museum.Health insurance supplemental allowanceReimbursement for training-related travel and conference attendance when program funding allows.What is the length of the appointment and potential start date?Appointments are for one year with potential renewal for one additional year.Start dates are flexible and coordinated with the selected candidate and mentors to ensure best outcomes. Selected fellows should plan to begin in the Summer of 2027.When are selections made?Selections will be made in April 2027. Nature of the AppointmentThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Any offer made is considered tentative, pending favorable outcome of the investigation.QualificationsTo be eligible, you must have earned your doctoral degree within five years of the appointment start date in one of the fields listed below. jobs.title: Animal Care and Training Internship at Navy Marine Mammal Program
jobs.description: Employer: Navy Marine Mammal Program Expires: 12/07/2026 The Navy Marine Mammal Program (MMP) began in 1959 with a single Navy scientist and one dolphin. Since that time, the program has expanded its study with the development of the Fleet Marine Mammal Systems utilizing dolphins, beluga whales, and sea lions. In addition, the MMP is doing a variety of research projects investigating the hearing abilities in a number of species of marine mammals. Research studying dolphin’s biosonar, and their physiological environmental adaptations are also being conducted. We are currently offering positions to be a part of the marine mammal program through internship opportunities. This internship is designed to give undergraduate students a dynamic educational experience in the marine mammal field while offering valuable career experience. Students will be responsible for a number of support tasks with dolphins and sea lions throughout the course of the internship. These responsibilities will include diet preparation, sanitation, and equipment and facility maintenance. Interns may also have the opportunity to assist the marine mammal training staff in husbandry and open ocean training. In addition, they will provide support to the animal care staff in animal physicals, and assist in a number of different marine mammal research projects. Lectures and field trips will also be conducted throughout the term to enhance the learning experience. The internship is offered on a competitive basis to sophomores, juniors, and seniors in the Marine Science, Biology, Zoology, Psychology, and Veterinary fields. Though the internship is designed for undergraduate students, recent graduates are also eligible to apply. All interns must arrange to receive college credit to be considered for the internship. The internship is a 40 hours per week, 16-week commitment. Interested students are encouraged to send a resume, cover letter, an unofficial or official copy of their transcripts, proof of medical insurance, and proof of US citizenship. In addition, a minimum of three letters of recommendation from professors or employers is necessary to complete the application. The application deadline for spring is October 1st, summer is March 1st, and Fall is June 1st. Please email all application materials directly to Erika Putman at Erika.Putman@NMMF.org. Currently, thanks to a generous grant from the Conrad Prebys Foundation, the National Marine Mammal Foundation will provide a stipend of $4,000 per semester to each intern to help defer the costs of participating in the program. We anticipate offering this stipend beginning with the Spring 2026 semester and continuing through the Fall 2027 semester. We hope this will encourage candidates to apply who could not previously due to financial constraints. If you would like to learn more about the MMP, we encourage you to visit our website at https://www.niwcpacific.navy.mil/About/Departments/Intelligence-Surveillance-and-Reconnaissance/Marine-Mammal-Program/. If you have any further questions, please feel free to contact Erika Putman at (619) 767-4100, or email at Erika.Putman@NMMF.org.

We’re home to the #1 wine and spirits brands in the U.S. - Barefoot Wine & High Noon and are the official sponsors of the NFL, NHL, UFC, and PGA of America.View our Corporate Values and Mission Statement here.A Taste of What You’ll Do​Join our dynamic team as a Viticulture or Grape Breeding Research Intern and immerse yourself in the innovative world of wine grape production. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives drive our success. jobs.title: 2027 Buck Institute Summer Scholars Programs at The Buck Institute for Research on Aging
jobs.description: Employer: The Buck Institute for Research on Aging Expires: 12/09/2026 Program OverviewThe Buck Summer Scholars Program offers undergraduate students the opportunity to investigate critical molecular and biological drivers of aging and translate that research into new therapies that will improve healthspan. Summer Scholar participants will conduct biomedical research to combat diseases of aging, such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, cancer, macular degeneration, heart disease, and diabetes. Under the guidance of a scientific mentor, each Summer Scholar will be responsible for their own mentored research project. The Program emphasizes both laboratory and communication skills training to develop well-rounded future scientists, healthcare professionals, and policymakers. The Summer Scholars Program emphasizes the development of scientific communication and critical thinking skills in addition to laboratory skills. Throughout the summer, student participants will be guided through writing assignments that simulate research explanations scientists often must provide to other scientists, financial supporters, or the public. The communication training will culminate with presentations of their work to peers, mentors, and other scientists. Other program features include a flexible start date and eligibility for international students (via CPT) and graduating seniors to participate.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-_2r63wEfoA Virtual Informational SessionsInterested in learning more about the Buck’s postbaccalaureate and undergraduate summer research programs? Sessions will be held:Tuesday, November 3, 2026 | 4:30–5:30 p.m. PTTuesday, December 8, 2026 | 4:30–5:30 p.m. PT https://buckinstitute.zoom.us/j/87622293432Meeting ID: 876 2229 3432 Program Learning Objectives:Participants will:1. Plan and execute a mentored research project.2. Learn new technical skills.3. Explain scientific concepts to a lay audience.4. Give a formal research presentation to scientists. Job Qualifications:Please review the full Program Eligibility Requirements, project descriptions, desired skills, and application requirements at https://www.buckinstitute.org/education-training/undergraduate-postbacc/ before applying.Applicants must:Have completed at least one term at a university during the 2026-2027 academic year.Be legally able to receive a stipend (U.S. citizen, permanent resident, CPT, or similar work authorization).Have a GPA of 2.0 or higher.Have some prior biological, computational, or other relevant research experience. jobs.title: SPARK (Summer Program for the Advancement of Research Knowledge) at Moffitt Cancer Center
jobs.description: Employer: Moffitt Cancer Center Expires: 12/10/2026 The SPARK program was started in 1986 to allow undergraduate students the opportunity to train within the various specialties (Immunology, Mathematics, Machine Learning, Public Health, Drug Discovery, Molecular Oncology, etc.) of cancer research at the Moffitt Cancer Center. To date, we have hosted over 830 interns and are proud to continue training the next generation of researchers and physicians.We host interns in Moffitt labs for 10 weeks over the summer, while they work on various project with the assistance of their mentors. Upon the conclusion of the program, students present their findings at Research Day. To prepare the interns, we have a weekly scientific communications class. This helps the interns get comfortable with their material and presenting in front of others.Applicants must be 18 and a US Citizen. Unfortunately, we are unable to accept international students. The program does not provide housing, for this reason most of our successful applicants are local to the Tampa Bay area.Apply now! Application closes January 6th, 2027. Email SPARK@moffitt.org with any questions.
