jobs.title: Ag Dealer Internship at PrairieLand Partners
jobs.description: Employer: PrairieLand Partners Expires: 12/10/2026 Get more than an internship. Get an inside look at the agriculture industry.Are you a college student looking to turn your classroom knowledge into real-world experience? Join AgriVision Equipment Group & PrairieLand Partners (AVE-PLP) for a summer internship designed to give you a behind-the-scenes look at how a John Deere dealership operates.You won’t be stuck doing one task all summer. As an Ag Dealer Intern, you’ll rotate through Parts, Sales, and Service work alongside experienced dealership professionals, interact with customers, and get hands-on exposure to the people, technology, and equipment that keep agriculture moving. What Makes This Internship Different?This isn’t just about checking a box for school.We view every intern as a potential future member of our team. Your experience will be designed to complement your education, help you explore career options, and give you a better understanding of where you could fit in the agriculture industry.During your internship, you’ll have the opportunity to: Get hands-on exposure to Service and see how technicians diagnose, repair, and support modern agricultural equipment.Learn how Sales works - from customer relationships to equipment solutions and technology. Experience Parts and learn how dealerships keep customers and technicians moving.Work directly with employees, managers, and customers. See how a John Deere dealership supports farmers and agricultural operations.Learn about precision agriculture, technology, equipment, and business operations.Explore different career paths within the agriculture equipment industry.Build professional skills and relationships that can help launch your career after graduation. Who are we looking for?We're looking for students who are: Currently pursuing a degree in Agriculture, Agribusiness, Agricultural Business, Operations Management, Business Administration, Agricultural Production Operations, Precision Agriculture, Sales or a related field. Interested in building a career in agriculture and/or the equipment industry. Curious, motivated, adaptable, and willing to learn.Comfortable working with different people and in different environments.Willing and able to relocate for the summer. In good academic standing with a minimum 2.75 GPA.Have at least one semester remaining after the internship.Have a valid driver's license and reliable transportation.Previous experience with large agricultural equipment, John Deere equipment, commercial/turf equipment, or dealerships is a plus - but it is NOT required. We can teach you the equipment and the industry. We're looking for students who bring the right attitude, curiosity, and willingness to learn. About AVE-PLP: AgriVision Equipment Group & PrairieLand Partners (AVE-PLP) is a joint venture between two leading John Deere dealerships. Together, we support customers across Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, and Missouri and are committed to leading agriculture in rural America.Our team is built around Integrity, Servant Leadership, Courageous Innovation, and Performance and we're looking for the next generation of agriculture leaders to join us. Ready to Get Started?Your summer internship can be more than a line on your résumé.Come spend the summer learning how agriculture, technology, equipment, and business come together and start building the career you want.Apply today and tell us where you want to go next.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Graduate Internship – Data Science at Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Expires: 12/10/2026 Summer 2027 Graduate Internship – Data Science The Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Graduate Intern Program in Data Science is intended to introduce full-time or part-time graduate students to the broader Federal Reserve System and, more specifically, the use of data science in the Banking Supervision function. Being at the forefront of overseeing the nation’s largest and most complex financial institutions is a unique opportunity that requires highly analytical and quantitative individuals.The Grad Intern Program provides an opportunity to work in an intellectually stimulating and collaborative environment, to engage in meaningful public service, and to interact with senior leaders at the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis and across the Federal Reserve System. Interns will receive on-the-job mentoring and professional development as they engage in job duties.APPLICATION CLOSES Sunday, December 6th, 2026, at Midnight.We are looking for students who are willing to work 40 hours/week for 12 weeks beginning May 24th, 2027 through August 13th, 2027. Rate of pay is $27.00/hour. This position requires a regular on-site presence.Program Description: Learn to manage, manipulate, interpret, and analyze trends in large sets of data and methodology documents. Enhance knowledge in programming and the software development life cycle. Handle and summarize large amounts of macroeconomic and banking data. Become familiar with different metrics and measures that are used to evaluate the health of the banking system. Synthesize information and glean insights related to banking conditions around the country. Present technical issues to non-technical audiences and clearly articulate findings in verbal and written form. Utilize advanced statistical techniques to analyze conditions in the banking sector, or across various industries or communities. Participate in internal networking and mentorship opportunities with quantitative staff and leadership across the Federal Reserve System.Required Qualifications: Currently enrolled and actively pursuing a graduate degree in a quantitative field such as (but not limited to) Computer Science, Data Science, Economics, Engineering, Finance, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, etc. Strong academic record in MS or Ph.D. program. Knowledge of query languages such as SQL. Demonstrated experience with R or Python. Code samples will be requested from selected candidates. Ability to work collaboratively within a team. Meet Protected Individual requirement. Able to work 40 hours per week throughout the duration of the 12-week internship program, starting in May 2027.Additional Preferred Qualifications (Not Required): Knowledge of R Shiny dashboard building and reporting experience using R Markdown. Knowledge of collaborative version control platforms such as GitLab. Knowledge of Finance and Banking. Knowledge of Data Visualization.Please note: We do NOT provide relocation assistance, housing, travel reimbursement, or sponsorship. jobs.title: 2027 AKS Development Services Internship Program at AKS Engineering & Forestry LLC
jobs.description: Employer: AKS Engineering & Forestry LLC - AKS Expires: 12/10/2026 Go Beyond the Classroom Looking to build real-world experience this summer? The AKS Internship Program gives college students the chance to apply what they’re learning in the classroom, build practical skills, and contribute in a professional environment. Through meaningful project experience and a supportive team setting, interns gain confidence, broaden their understanding of the industry, and take important steps toward career readiness. How it WorksEach internship experience may look a little different depending on the role and team, but every internship is designed to help students learn by doing. Interns gain hands-on experience through real work, connect with professionals across AKS, and get a better understanding of how different disciplines contribute to project outcomes. For students who return, each summer can build on the last with new experiences, added responsibility, and a deeper understanding of areas that interest them. Participation is a one-summer commitment at a time. Students who are interested in returning are encouraged to express interest, and continued participation depends on performance, program fit, and available positions. Who You AreTo be considered for this internship program, students should: Be currently enrolled in an accredited 2- or 4-year program with a declared major in Business, Finance, Real Estate, Engineering, Urban Planning, Environmental Sciences, Geographic Information Systems, or similar. Have completed at least one year of college before the internship start date Maintain a GPA of 3.0 or higher Be available to work full-time for 12 weeks during the summer Be able to work from the Las Vegas, NV, or Phoenix, AZ, offices, where this program is offered What You’ll LearnEnergy Project Development: Gain an understanding of how utility-scale solar, wind, battery energy storage, transmission, and other energy infrastructure projects progress from early-stage development toward construction, including an introduction to roles associated with permitting, real estate, environmental, interconnection, and project management of energy projects. Research, Mapping, & Due Diligence: Build practical experience researching project sites, environmental factors, property ownership, zoning, infrastructure, permitting requirements, and other development considerations while using tools such as Google Earth, ArcGIS, KMZ files, and Microsoft Office suite to organize and visualize information. Project Management & Professional Communication: Learn how development teams manage project information, schedules, action items, documentation, and deliverables while developing skills in interacting and communicating within a professional environment, preparing project summaries, technical memoranda, presentations, and other professional materials. Day in the Life (Examples)Work under the direction of a Project Manager or Assistant Project Manager and alongside the Development Services team to gain hands-on experience in a client-focused consulting environment. Interns can expect to work approximately 40-50 hours per week while contributing to project work and day-to-day team priorities. Responsibilities may include: Conducting research and assisting with desktop due diligence related to energy projects, including property ownership, zoning, permitting, utilities, transmission, infrastructure, environmental constraints, and other development considerations. Creating and maintaining project maps, KMZ files, spreadsheets, and other project materials while compiling and organizing information from public databases, agencies, utilities, and other sources. Assisting with project documentation and deliverables, including project summaries, technical memoranda, presentations, meeting materials, action-item tracking, and project files. Participating in project meetings, site visits, industry events, and other activities while collaborating with Project Managers, Assistant Project Managers, and other team members. We Have Your Back At AKS, interns are supported throughout the summer. Each intern is paired with a mentor and receives direction from a supervisor who guides assignments and project work. That supervisor may vary depending on the projects involved. Throughout the internship, interns receive regular feedback to support learning, growth, and professional development. At the end of the summer, each intern participates in a final evaluation to reflect on their experience, discuss future goals, and explore the possibility of returning for another internship, based on performance and available openings. Earn While You Learn This is a paid internship, and interns are compensated for their time and contributions. Pay is provided on an hourly basis, with overtime paid at one and a half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a week. The typical pay range for this position is $19 to $25 per hour. Time off may be requested in advance, but it is unpaid.
